basics.description: Deploy the **M365 Copilot Usage Reporter** to Azure Container Apps. It pulls prebuilt public images, provisions a PostgreSQL flexible server, and serves the dashboard on a public HTTPS endpoint. You only need to set an admin password.

basics.name: namePrefix
basics.label: Resource name prefix
basics.toolTip: Short prefix (lowercase, starts with a letter) used to name every resource.

validations.message: 2-12 lowercase letters or numbers, starting with a letter.

options.text: [concat('This subscription cannot provision an Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server in "', location(), '", so the deployment would fail with "The value of the Version should be in: []". Pick a different region above (e.g. australiaeast, eastus, or westeurope). If every region you try shows this, register the Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL resource provider on the subscription and retry.')]

elements.name: adminUsername
elements.label: Dashboard admin username
elements.toolTip: Username for the first sign-in to the dashboard.

validations.message: 3-32 characters: letters, numbers, dot, underscore or hyphen.

elements.name: adminPassword
elements.toolTip: Password for the first sign-in. Use at least 8 characters with a mix of types.

options.text: Defaults are fine for most deployments. If deployment fails with "The value of the 'Version' should be in: []", your subscription is not permitted to create a PostgreSQL flexible server in the selected region — change the region on the Basics tab (the form warns you there). The version/size options below rarely need changing.

elements.name: imageTag
elements.label: Image tag
elements.toolTip: Container image tag to deploy (e.g. 'latest' or a version tag).

elements.name: postgresVersion
elements.label: PostgreSQL version
elements.toolTip: PostgreSQL major version to provision. 16 is the recommended default.

elements.name: postgresSkuTier
elements.label: Database compute tier
elements.toolTip: Burstable is cheapest. Switch to General Purpose if your region lacks Burstable capacity.

elements.name: postgresSkuName
elements.label: Database compute size
elements.toolTip: Must match the tier above. Examples: Standard_B1ms (Burstable), Standard_D2ds_v5 (General Purpose), Standard_E2ds_v5 (Memory Optimized).

validations.message: A valid flexible-server SKU name, e.g. Standard_B1ms.

options.text: By default the dashboard is protected by the admin password you set. You can additionally enable Entra ID single sign-on so colleagues can view it with their work account (read-only). You can turn this on now, or later from the api Container App's Authentication blade — leave it off to decide later.

elements.name: enableEntraAuth
elements.label: Enable Entra ID single sign-on
elements.toolTip: When enabled, signed-in Entra users get a read-only viewer role. Administration stays behind the password.

elements.name: entraClientId
elements.label: App registration client ID
elements.toolTip: Application (client) ID of the Entra app registration used for sign-in. You can reuse the reporter's own app registration.

elements.name: entraClientSecret
elements.toolTip: A client secret value for the sign-in app registration.

elements.name: entraTenantId
elements.label: Directory (tenant) ID
elements.toolTip: Tenant that issues sign-in tokens. Defaults to the deployment tenant.

options.text: After deployment, add the redirect URI shown in the deployment's 'entraRedirectUriToRegister' output to your app registration (Authentication → Web). If you gate access by a security group, also add a groups claim under the app registration's Token configuration.
